/**
 * struct usb_interface - what usb device drivers talk to
 * @altsetting: array of interface structures, one for each alternate
 *	setting that may be selected.  Each one includes a set of
 *	endpoint configurations.  They will be in no particular order.
 * @cur_altsetting: the current altsetting.
 * @num_altsetting: number of altsettings defined.
 * @intf_assoc: interface association descriptor
 * @minor: the minor number assigned to this interface, if this
 *	interface is bound to a driver that uses the USB major number.
 *	If this interface does not use the USB major, this field should
 *	be unused.  The driver should set this value in the probe()
 *	function of the driver, after it has been assigned a minor
 *	number from the USB core by calling usb_register_dev().
 * @condition: binding state of the interface: not bound, binding
 *	(in probe()), bound to a driver, or unbinding (in disconnect())
 * @sysfs_files_created: sysfs attributes exist
 * @ep_devs_created: endpoint child pseudo-devices exist
 * @unregistering: flag set when the interface is being unregistered
 * @needs_remote_wakeup: flag set when the driver requires remote-wakeup
 *	capability during autosuspend.
 * @needs_altsetting0: flag set when a set-interface request for altsetting 0
 *	has been deferred.
 * @needs_binding: flag set when the driver should be re-probed or unbound
 *	following a reset or suspend operation it doesn't support.
 * @authorized: This allows to (de)authorize individual interfaces instead
 *	a whole device in contrast to the device authorization.
 * @wireless_status: if the USB device uses a receiver/emitter combo, whether
 *	the emitter is connected.
 * @wireless_status_work: Used for scheduling wireless status changes
 *	from atomic context.
 * @dev: driver model's view of this device
 * @usb_dev: if an interface is bound to the USB major, this will point
 *	to the sysfs representation for that device.
 * @reset_ws: Used for scheduling resets from atomic context.
 * @resetting_device: USB core reset the device, so use alt setting 0 as
 *	current; needs bandwidth alloc after reset.
 *
 * USB device drivers attach to interfaces on a physical device.  Each
 * interface encapsulates a single high level function, such as feeding
 * an audio stream to a speaker or reporting a change in a volume control.
 * Many USB devices only have one interface.  The protocol used to talk to
 * an interface's endpoints can be defined in a usb "class" specification,
 * or by a product's vendor.  The (default) control endpoint is part of
 * every interface, but is never listed among the interface's descriptors.
 *
 * The driver that is bound to the interface can use standard driver model
 * calls such as dev_get_drvdata() on the dev member of this structure.
 *
 * Each interface may have alternate settings.  The initial configuration
 * of a device sets altsetting 0, but the device driver can change
 * that setting using usb_set_interface().  Alternate settings are often
 * used to control the use of periodic endpoints, such as by having
 * different endpoints use different amounts of reserved USB bandwidth.
 * All standards-conformant USB devices that use isochronous endpoints
 * will use them in non-default settings.
 *
 * The USB specification says that alternate setting numbers must run from
 * 0 to one less than the total number of alternate settings.  But some
 * devices manage to mess this up, and the structures aren't necessarily
 * stored in numerical order anyhow.  Use usb_altnum_to_altsetting() to
 * look up an alternate setting in the altsetting array based on its number.
 */
struct usb_interface {
	/* array of alternate settings for this interface,
	 * stored in no particular order */
	struct usb_host_interface *altsetting;

	struct usb_host_interface *cur_altsetting;	/* the currently
					 * active alternate setting */
	unsigned num_altsetting;	/* number of alternate settings */

#define USB_MAXENDPOINTS	30
/* this maximum is arbitrary */
#define USB_MAXINTERFACES	32
#define USB_MAXIADS		(USB_MAXINTERFACES/2)

/**
 * struct usb_interface_cache - long-term representation of a device interface
 * @num_altsetting: number of altsettings defined.
 * @ref: reference counter.
 * @altsetting: variable-length array of interface structures, one for
 *	each alternate setting that may be selected.  Each one includes a
 *	set of endpoint configurations.  They will be in no particular order.
 *
 * These structures persist for the lifetime of a usb_device, unlike
 * struct usb_interface (which persists only as long as its configuration
 * is installed).  The altsetting arrays can be accessed through these
 * structures at any time, permitting comparison of configurations and
 * providing support for the /sys/kernel/debug/usb/devices pseudo-file.
 */
struct usb_interface_cache {
	unsigned num_altsetting;	/* number of alternate settings */
	struct kref ref;		/* reference counter */

	/* variable-length array of alternate settings for this interface,
	 * stored in no particular order */
	struct usb_host_interface altsetting[];
};
#define	ref_to_usb_interface_cache(r) \
		container_of(r, struct usb_interface_cache, ref)
#define	altsetting_to_usb_interface_cache(a) \
		container_of(a, struct usb_interface_cache, altsetting[0])

/**
 * struct usb_host_config - representation of a device's configuration
 * @desc: the device's configuration descriptor.
 * @string: pointer to the cached version of the iConfiguration string, if
 *	present for this configuration.
 * @intf_assoc: list of any interface association descriptors in this config
 * @interface: array of pointers to usb_interface structures, one for each
 *	interface in the configuration.  The number of interfaces is stored
 *	in desc.bNumInterfaces.  These pointers are valid only while the
 *	configuration is active.
 * @intf_cache: array of pointers to usb_interface_cache structures, one
 *	for each interface in the configuration.  These structures exist
 *	for the entire life of the device.
 * @extra: pointer to buffer containing all extra descriptors associated
 *	with this configuration (those preceding the first interface
 *	descriptor).
 * @extralen: length of the extra descriptors buffer.
 *
 * USB devices may have multiple configurations, but only one can be active
 * at any time.  Each encapsulates a different operational environment;
 * for example, a dual-speed device would have separate configurations for
 * full-speed and high-speed operation.  The number of configurations
 * available is stored in the device descriptor as bNumConfigurations.
 *
 * A configuration can contain multiple interfaces.  Each corresponds to
 * a different function of the USB device, and all are available whenever
 * the configuration is active.  The USB standard says that interfaces
 * are supposed to be numbered from 0 to desc.bNumInterfaces-1, but a lot
 * of devices get this wrong.  In addition, the interface array is not
 * guaranteed to be sorted in numerical order.  Use usb_ifnum_to_if() to
 * look up an interface entry based on its number.
 *
 * Device drivers should not attempt to activate configurations.  The choice
 * of which configuration to install is a policy decision based on such
 * considerations as available power, functionality provided, and the user's
 * desires (expressed through userspace tools).  However, drivers can call
 * usb_reset_configuration() to reinitialize the current configuration and
 * all its interfaces.
 */
struct usb_host_config {
	struct usb_config_descriptor	desc;

	char *string;		/* iConfiguration string, if present */

	/* List of any Interface Association Descriptors in this
	 * configuration. */
	struct usb_interface_assoc_descriptor *intf_assoc[USB_MAXIADS];

	/* the interfaces associated with this configuration,
	 * stored in no particular order */
	struct usb_interface *interface[USB_MAXINTERFACES];

	/* Interface information available even when this is not the
	 * active configuration */
	struct usb_interface_cache *intf_cache[USB_MAXINTERFACES];

	unsigned char *extra;   /* Extra descriptors */
	int extralen;
};

#define usb_actconfig_show(field, format_string)			\
static ssize_t field##_show(struct device *dev,				\
			    struct device_attribute *attr, char *buf)	\
{									\
	struct usb_device *udev;					\
	struct usb_host_config *actconfig;				\
	ssize_t rc;							\
									\
	udev = to_usb_device(dev);					\
	rc = usb_lock_device_interruptible(udev);			\
	if (rc < 0)							\
		return -EINTR;						\
	actconfig = udev->actconfig;					\
	if (actconfig)							\
		rc = sysfs_emit(buf, format_string,			\
				actconfig->desc.field);			\
	usb_unlock_device(udev);					\
	return rc;							\
}									\

#define usb_descriptor_attr_le16(field, format_string)			\
static ssize_t								\
field##_show(struct device *dev, struct device_attribute *attr,	\
		char *buf)						\
{									\
	struct usb_device *udev;					\
									\
	udev = to_usb_device(dev);					\
	return sysfs_emit(buf, format_string,				\
			le16_to_cpu(udev->descriptor.field));		\
}									\
static DEVICE_ATTR_RO(field)

usb_descriptor_attr_le16(idVendor, "%04x\n");
usb_descriptor_attr_le16(idProduct, "%04x\n");

ATTRS = ("idVendor", "idProduct", "bConfigurationValue", "speed")
EPATTRS = ("bEndpointAddress", "bmAttributes", "wMaxPacketSize")

def script(nonce):
    assert re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{32}", nonce)
    cmd = (f"echo K76MD_BEGIN_{nonce}; echo FDS; /bin/busybox ls -l /proc/1/fd; r=$?; echo FD_RC:$r; "
           "for f in idVendor idProduct bConfigurationValue speed; do echo ATTR:$f; "
           "/bin/busybox cat /sys/bus/usb/devices/1-1/$f || r=1; done; "
           "for e in ep_01 ep_81; do for f in bEndpointAddress bmAttributes wMaxPacketSize; "
           "do echo EP:$e:$f; /bin/busybox cat /sys/bus/usb/devices/1-1:1.0/$e/$f || r=1; done; done; "
           "if test -L /sys/bus/usb/devices/1-1:1.0/driver; then r=1; fi; "
           f"echo K76MD_DONE_{nonce}:$r")
    assert len(cmd.encode()) <= 950 and not any(c in cmd for c in "\r\n\0")
    return cmd


def parse(text, nonce):
    lines = text.replace("\r", "").splitlines()
    begin, done = f"K76MD_BEGIN_{nonce}", f"K76MD_DONE_{nonce}:0"
    assert lines.count(begin) == 1 and lines.count(done) == 1
    start, end = lines.index(begin), lines.index(done)
    assert start < end and lines[start + 1] == "FDS"
    assert all(line == "" for line in lines[:start])
    assert lines[end + 1:] == ["# "]
    data = lines[start + 2:end]
    assert data.count("FD_RC:0") == 1
    split = data.index("FD_RC:0")
    result = radio_receipt.parse_parent_fds("\n".join(data[:split]))
    rest = data[split + 1:]
    expected = [("ATTR:" + key, value) for key, value in zip(ATTRS, ("a012", "8400", "1", "480"))]
    for ep, address in (("ep_01", "01"), ("ep_81", "81")):
        expected.extend((f"EP:{ep}:{key}", value) for key, value in zip(EPATTRS, (address, "02", "0200")))
    assert len(rest) == len(expected) * 2
    for i, (key, value) in enumerate(expected): assert rest[2 * i:2 * i + 2] == [key, value]
    return dict(result, owned_a012_8400_config1_speed480=True, bulk_OUT01_IN81_maxpacket512=True,
                no_bound_USB_interface_driver=True)

# RAM76 resume21a — metadata-before / public receipt review

2026-10-21; independent source-only lane. **NO-GO as written for the requested
strict metadata-before admission**, pending B1/B2 below. Query semantics and the
normal protocol grammar are source-supported; the nine supplied host tests pass.
This is not a native failure or permission to try an effectful operation.

Owned changes: this report and fresh `metadata-review/` only. No production source,
central document, index or build edits. No UART/RPC/status/target/network/private
capture access, firmware execution or build occurred. Parent reports resume21a
boot and fixed postcheck PASS, with no radio command yet; this reviewer inspected
their public receipts, not the live target. Prior native directboot is unrelated.
Only `--before-native-load` is reviewed for entry. The after-mode and an effectful
trial wrapper are **not approved** by this report.

## Findings requiring closure before metadata TX

### B1 — FD parser violates no-extra-lines/source-exact acceptance

`radio_receipt.py:90–99` silently discards **any number of `total N` lines in any
position**, and `.strip()` removes leading/trailing blank FD lines. A6 has
`CONFIG_DESKTOP=n`: retained `coreutils/ls.c:1025–1037` compiles the `total` output
out entirely. Inserting `total 0` after `FDS`, twice or between FD entries still
passes the present parser by direct source inspection. These are not legitimate
lines for this fixed query, and must not be silently filtered into success.

The FD regex also accepts arbitrary `l`-prefixed tokens and unconstrained middle
text rather than the actual A6 long-listing structure. For example, four lines
`ls: unexpected N -> /dev/console` for N=0..3 satisfy the regex without being FD
listings. Existing fixtures cover duplicate FD numbers, missing/extra FDs and a
watchdog FD, but not these accepted malformed/extra-line cases.

Required: exact four source-compatible long-listing records, FD numbers0..3 once
each, console/ttyAK0 targets only; reject extra/blank/`total`/malformed lines. Add
negative fixtures for these cases and a fixture representing **actual A6 output**,
not just desktop-style UID/GID/date columns. A6 has username/timestamp/color
features disabled: `ls -l` itself omits user/group fields without `-n`; see
`ls.c:511–589`. Do not change the target command merely to fit a desktop fixture.

### B2 — the before-mode does not itself enforce the complete exact21a handoff

`metadata21a.py:90–108` checks both public image hashes, the postcheck PASS state,
live recorder part/sole owner/lifetime, PID/start identity and cumulative TX. But
it omits checks already present in the fixed postcheck's own admission:

- boot receipt state `RAM76_BOOT_AND_INERT_MONITOR_OBSERVED` and receipt part;
- postcheck part;
- private boot checkpoint `image_sha256`, `part`, `monitor_observed is True`,
  `shell_started is False` and explicit integer/nonnegative cursor validation;
- exact boolean type for `one_empty_monitor_refresh` (currently coerced by `int`);
- binding of the imported `postcheck.py` to the postcheck receipt's
  `recipe_sha256` **before** executing its module and using its query table.

This is an incomplete self-contained admission gate, **not evidence that the
parent's observed boot/postcheck was wrong**. Public receipts currently have the
expected states/parts; the postcheck recipe hash matches the reviewed file.
The reviewer did not read the private checkpoint. Restore those explicit checks,
or have the parent document an equally exact frozen external admission that
supplies them; do not infer the omitted facts from filenames or mutable imports.

The correctly derived postcheck increment is **320 TX bytes for14 commands**, plus
exactly one byte iff the admitted boolean refresh is true. The inspected public
postcheck has that flag true, so this before-mode expects **boot checkpoint TX+321**.
No private counter value is exported here. Require exact equality and no other
sender; never adjust a checkpoint to make a mismatched counter pass.

## 6. P4: exact allocation/probe and normal retirement (S5)

Proposed next derivative owner: mainly `utils/if_usb.c`, `hgic_smac/{core.c,hgics.h,
procfs.c,procfs.h}`, `utils/{fwctrl.c,fwctrl.h}` and minimal bus receipt declarations.
Keep16 TX/32 RX/2560B RX backing, not increased counts/ceilings. Public-source
facts requiring fault closure:

- `if_usb.c:365–409`: partial topology gate but no exact interface/alt/endpoint
  count, unique OUT01/IN81, bulk512 HS configuration validation before allocation/
  submission. Use source-supported expected descriptors + later private current
  descriptor continuity, not guessed interface numbers. Reject missing/duplicate/
  wrong endpoints/maxpacket before TX padding's ep_out_size division/alignment use.
- `qinit:124–155`: partial counts accepted at `probe:415–419`; RX backing allocation
  failure at:140–144 frees buf **without usb_free_urb**. Require exactly16+32 and
  rollback every successful prior allocation, including the current unlisted URB.
  `probe:421` ignores core-probe return; require both exact return and valid context.
- `core_probe:1140–1218`: early hghw mismatch can call core_remove before works/
  timers/ctrl are initialized; later fwctrl workqueue failure is not propagated.
  Track initialized stages so cleanup never touches an uninitialized primitive.
- `if_usb.c:427–448`: after get_dev/set_intfdata, initial RX failure drains/removes/
  frees without clear-intfdata/put_dev; stale pointer/ref leak. Distinguish device
  reference actually acquired, intfdata actually published, callback context live.
  Every path clears publication before invalidating its object and puts exactly
  once. Do not infer core lifetime merely from nonnull bus_priv after a failed probe.
- `submit_rx_urbs:210–221` drains rx_freeq while completions can resubmit/requeue;
  initialization must submit the finite initial32 slots once, not loop over an
  immediately replenished freeq forever. Separate list-used from HCD-inflight.

**Required ordering:** serialize STOP/no-new-TX/RX/worker admission → hold valid
context/URB references → kill/drain submitted URBs **outside qlock** → cancel/join
init/TX/detect/test/fwctrl work and timers with no requeue → unregister DOWN hw/
remove proc access and pending waiters → purge only locally owned queues → free
backing/core/bus and drop dev refs. Review exact ordering dependencies (especially
workers waiting on controls); cancellation must wake/error only live owned waiters,
never make shutdown depend on already-disabled RX. Existing USB quiesce before
core_remove (`:451–468`) is valuable but not proof that concurrent worker submit
cannot race the drain. Unlink under qlock (`:62–72`) is not synchronous retirement.
K/`drivers/usb/core/urb.c:678–721` guarantees idle after kill returns, forbids holding
callback locks, and contains an **unbounded wait** at:718. A blocked kill/cancel is
not permission to force free; prearmed watchdog may expire instead.

**Counter/lifetime requirement:** reserve inflight ownership and callback refs
BEFORE entering submit; callback can run before submit returns. Submit-error
rollback and successful immediate callback must be disjoint owners; no increment
after callback leading to phantom inflight, double decrement, token return or ref
drop. Keep submitters-in-progress separately from submitted-not-completed and
callbacks-active: an empty used list/inflight0 alone does not prove callbacks have
returned. Resubmission creates another owned interval; STOP fences that transition.
RX/TX submit-attempt/accepted/failed/completed/cancel totals reconcile per generation,
not from current status rebasing. Overflow/negative/impossible totals fail closed.

## Request, queue and ref conservation

`owned_control.h:19–35` embeds the completion/list/response in one heap allocation,
bounded statically to1024B; skb cb stores a fitting copied heap-request pointer.
No async pointer names the init caller's24B output, a stack response or completion.
`owned_control.c:90–133` constructs WAITER privately, then adds REGISTRY before
publication under owner→receipt locks. Allocation/admission failure frees only
the never-published constructor allocation.

| Role | Actual selected acquire / release |
|---|---|
| WAITER | Constructor:105–106; do_cmd's final waiter_done at fwctrl.c:156, owned_control.c:381–387. |
| REGISTRY | create:123–125; only final owner_release:398–432 after actual P4a return proofs. |
| PENDING | publish:162–163; exact list removal/ref release:372–378, under ctrl lock. RX borrows only while holding that same lock. |
| QUEUE | publish:164–166; exact UNSENT cancel:52–60, or atomic transfer to WORKER:184–187. |
| WORKER | take:184–187 transfers the queue ref, not an extra inc/dec; worker_done:217–224 follows abort or transport return. |
| SUBMITTER | claim:254 before USB; submit_result:281 only on actual submit return. |
